name: ipv4-name-constraint-non-canonical-cidr-valid
description: permittedSubtrees iPAddress encodes a non-canonical IPv4 CIDR: address 192.168.1.1 with mask /24, so the host bits (the trailing .1) are non-zero. RFC 5280 4.2.1.10 describes the iPAddress constraint as an OCTET STRING that 'specifies a subnet'; applying the mask to the encoded address is the only sensible interpretation. The leaf SAN 192.168.1.5 is inside the intended 192.168.1.0/24 subnet, so the cert must be accepted. Botan <3.12 stored the constraint without masking off host bits, so 192.168.1.1/24 would only match 192.168.1.1 exactly — a leaf for any other host in the subnet was incorrectly rejected, and any leaf address whose unmasked bytes happened to equal the constraint's stored bytes was incorrectly accepted.
references: Botan 304d88db70 — Normalize IPv4 addresses in name constraints
notes: cryptography's IPv4Network constructor with strict=True would refuse 192.168.1.1/24 and with strict=False would silently normalize away the host bits. Inject the raw NameConstraints DER via unknown_extensions to preserve the non-canonical encoding.
ascii2der payload: NC SEQUENCE { permittedSubtrees [0] { GeneralSubtree { iPAddress [7 PRIMITIVE] address||mask } } } where the OCTET STRING contents are c0a80101 (192.168.1.1) || ffffff00 (/24).
